title: Introduce subtle hover affordances and smart reflow for very wide/very dense tables
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our virtualized table components are hard to scan and interact with at high row densities and in very wide datasets. Column grips are visually subtle and discoverability drops on touch/trackpad devices. When space is constrained we use full column collapse rules but we see layout jumps and loss of context. This ticket proposes a combined pattern: (1) introduce a subtle hover/touch affordance that reveals actionable controls (resize grip, sort, filter) without increasing visual noise; (2) add a smart reflow strategy that progressively hides low-priority columns into a "more" menu and provides inline context summaries to avoid losing important signals; (3) provide a multi-handle column grip mode for efficient resizing of adjacent groups; and (4) ensure keyboard and screen-reader parity for all interactions. The goal is to reduce input friction, avoid layout jank during reflow, and keep important columns visible by priority while preserving the performance characteristics of virtualization.
acceptance_criteria: Hover/touch affordance appears within 160ms of pointer hover or first touch and does not re-render the entire table viewport
Resize grip is discoverable at small densities (compact and micro) without increasing row height
Smart reflow collapses pre-defined low-priority columns into a single overflow menu with accessible labels and preserves sort/filter state
Multi-handle resize allows adjusting an adjacent column group by dragging once; operation is undoable via escape and reflected in layout tokens
Keyboard nav: header affordances reachable by Tab, sortable by Enter/Space, resize via arrow keys with modifier (Shift+Arrow), and screen reader announces collapse/restore operations
Performance: no measurable increase in first-paint or scroll frame drop rate in the virtualized viewport (within 2% baseline) for 50k-row datasets
tasks: Audit existing header affordances across table variants and density tokens
Prototype hover affordance styles in Figma and generate token proposals for hover radius, contrast, and motion durations
Design smart reflow priority schema and a lightweight collapsed menu pattern with breadcrumb context
Design multi-handle grip visuals and interaction model including long-press behavior for touch
Work with frontend eng to implement minimal DOM updates and test with virtualization (avoid re-mounting rows)
Write accessibility spec and keyboard mapping; validate with accessibility QA
Create test harness to measure perf impact and document thresholds
Gather feedback in design review and iterate on visuals and labels
decisions: Use subtle semi-transparent overlay on hover instead of new iconography to reduce visual noise
Smart reflow will be driven by a prioritized column metadata list supplied by consumers; design will supply defaults for common tables
Multi-handle will be a mode toggled via long-press on the grip for touch and via modifier key (Alt) for pointer to avoid accidental mass resizes
Collapsed columns will preserve filter and sort state and surface a one-row summary in the overflow menu
Performance constraint: avoid triggering layout reflow across the entire table; update only header cells and the overflow anchor element
